reviews.title: 3rd Bandlab Review
reviews.text:
I remember leaving a 5 star review for this app years ago maybe around 2022 and quite frankly it's depressing how much that's changed nowadays. It's a shame to see the app that inspired me to start making music and had made it accessible to so many start shooting all of what made it great in the foot for the name of corporate greed.
The flood of ads is a direct insult to everyone who just wants to make art without having distractions forced into their face.
The pushing of AI tools is a direct insult to all real human artists.
The everconstricting paywalls are a direct insult to everyone who came here hoping to make their dreams on their limited budget.
From August 2020, back when I was just 12, to early 2025 this app has been my main way of making music and beloved by me, but the ad invasion left me looking for other options and my ability to make music has been wholly stagnated since this app began to fall apart. I was over halfway done with an album I was working on here but it has still not finished as the modern state of things has completely diswayed me from bothering with you. Using your desktop version is completely hopeless, the audio crackles to inaudability and runs slower than a slug.
So I leave this review and still check up on this app in the naïve hope that something can still change here for the better and fix the insulting, degrading changes made to it in recent times. Please don't continue down the road you've
chosen and reconcider the modern direction of you

reviews.title: Historic Falloff
reviews.text: I used to love this app. I used this app so much from middle-2020, and my capabilities grew as I used this app. BandLab had such good updates until around 2023, which is when you guys introduced your subscription service. Over time, features people could use without paying slowly got turned into things only people who paid money for the app could use. It has gotten to the point to where users cannot even make their own effects without a subscription, which is what prompted me to finally write this review. I have never written a negative review until today. This app is not the music creation app many other users and I used to use. It has become an app solely focused on making a profit, and I cannot continue to use this app after writing this review unless free users are given back the features they once had. If anyone is thinking about using this app: Don’t. Use another app such as GarageBand or FL Studio where at least the money you spend will be worth something. For the people behind BandLab: Do better.

reviews.title: Unfortunate Update
reviews.text: Having used BandLab on and off over the past several years, I was disappointed at what I came back to. BandLab was always my go to when it came to making music on my phone. It really was the best option when it came to free or cheap music production softwares you could go with. I never used the app consistently but whenever I had an itch to make music, I always went with BandLab. Having not opened the app in a while, I logged on again to be incredibly disappointed by the paywall behind the loops. The massive collection of free loops is what drew me to BandLab in the first place. I understand they need to make a profit, however, requiring a membership for these loops defeats what made the app so great for many of us, who wanted to produce music on a budget. Now, you are incredibly limited in what you can do, and when looking at the membership price, you might as well look elsewhere as there are stronger alternatives in a similar price range. It is truly unfortunate as this app was really great until recently.

reviews.title: Feedback from a long time BandLab user about paywalls and accessibility
reviews.text:
Message:
Hello BandLab team,

I have been using BandLab for a while and really appreciated how it made music creation accessible to everyone, especially independent or broke artists like myself who do not have access to expensive studio gear or software.

Lately I have become very disappointed to see more and more essential tools and features locked behind paywalls. The app now feels much harder to use freely than before, and the yearly subscription cost is too high for many up and coming creators who helped make BandLab popular in the first place.

BandLab built its reputation on being the free and open platform for all musicians. By putting so many creative tools behind a membership it risks losing that identity and many loyal users in the process.

Please reconsider how many core features are paywalled, or explore fairer pricing options so creators on tight budgets can still make great music. We value what BandLab offers, we just want it to stay true to its roots, creativity for everyone, not just those who can afford it.

I keep seeing BandLab advertise itself as a free platform that helps creators keep it free, yet the reality no longer matches that message. Asking for around £100 a year for full access makes the slogan feel misleading. For many of us independent artists, that is not free or accessible, it is the same problem that made us turn to BandLab in the first place.
